summary: Simulate collisions of asteroids moving along a line; positive moves right, negative left; the smaller explodes.
mainInsight: A stack holds surviving asteroids. A collision occurs only when the top is moving right (positive) and the incoming one is moving left (negative). Pop smaller tops, destroy both on a tie, and push the incoming asteroid only if it survives.

approaches.name: Repeated pass simulation
approaches.summary: Scan for collisions until none remain.

approaches.name: Stack
approaches.summary: Resolve each incoming negative asteroid against the top of the stack.

personalSolution.approach: Stack; pop smaller right-movers, then handle the tie and the survive-or-explode decision
personalSolution.notes: Optimal. The post-loop branches (tie, then push if the top is a left-mover or the stack is empty) are correct but split the cases across two conditions; a single alive flag may read more clearly.

commonMistakes: Colliding two negatives or two positives

cards.answer: Stack of surviving asteroids: resolve each incoming left-moving asteroid against the top of the stack. Clue: Asteroids only interact when a right-moving one is followed by a left-moving one, and a new asteroid can only hit the most recent survivors, which is last-in-first-out.
keyPoints: Asteroids only interact when a right-moving one is followed by a left-moving one, and a new asteroid can only hit the most recent survivors, which is last-in-first-out.
cards.explanation: Each incoming asteroid fights only the nearest surviving right-mover, so a stack of survivors resolves all collisions in one pass.

promptVariants: Which data structure resolves chain collisions in one pass?
How do you decide whether two neighbouring asteroids collide?
options: A stack; collide when the top is positive and the new one negative
A queue; collide when the front and back differ in sign each time
A min-heap by size; always collide the two smallest asteroids first
A hash map from size to count; cancel equal sizes with each other
cards.answer: A stack; collide when the top is positive and the new one negative
cards.explanation: Only a right-mover followed by a left-mover can meet.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A queue; collide when the front and back: Asteroids interact with their neighbours, not the ends.
incorrectOptionExplanations.A min-heap by size; always collide the t: Position order matters, not size order.

promptVariants: Why does each asteroid need a while loop against the stack?
What are the three outcomes of a collision?
cards.answer: A single left-moving asteroid may destroy several right-moving asteroids in a row, so it must keep colliding with the new top until it is destroyed, ties with it, or the top is no longer a right-mover. The outcomes are: the incoming one explodes, the top explodes (pop and continue), or both explode (pop and stop).
cards.explanation: Amortised O(n) because each asteroid is popped at most once.

promptVariants: In your loop, why does the last branch test `stack[-1] < 0` (or an empty stack) before pushing a?
After the while loop and the equality check, when is it correct to append the left-moving asteroid?
options: The top is a left-mover or nothing is left, so no collision can happen
The top is a right-mover that was smaller, so the incoming one survives
The top has the same size and both asteroids must be kept on the stack
The incoming asteroid always survives, so the test is only a safety check
cards.answer: The top is a left-mover or nothing is left, so no collision can happen
cards.explanation: After popping smaller right-movers, the top is either a larger right-mover (the incoming asteroid explodes and is not pushed), an equal one (both explode, handled by the equality branch), or a left-mover or nothing, in which case there is no collision and a survives.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The top is a right-mover that was smalle: Smaller right-movers were already popped by the while loop.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The top has the same size and both aster: Equal sizes destroy each other, handled by the equality branch.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The incoming asteroid always survives, s: A larger right-mover on top destroys it, so the test is essential.

cards.explanation: Every asteroid is pushed once and popped at most once.

promptVariants: Which input leaves every asteroid in place with no collisions?
When can two asteroids never meet?
cards.explanation: Left-movers drift away from the right-movers that follow them, so no pair ever approaches. Any right-mover followed later by a left-mover will collide.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[2, 3, -4, -5]: right-movers first, left: -4 meets 3, and so on; collisions happen.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[3, -3, 4, -4]: alternating directions w: Each pair collides and both explode.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[5, -2, 3, -1]: alternating directions o: Each left-mover hits the right-mover before it.
